bounded_admission.note: capacity = batch_limit × QUEUE_SLACK (2). A submission that finds the queue full is refused onto the direct path under the same core lock with its normal durability — never dropped, never a false success.

arms.adaptive_linger: group commit on; group_commit_batch=64; GroupCommitLinger::Adaptive (the deadline-aware rule)
arms.fixed_linger: group commit on; group_commit_batch=64; GroupCommitLinger::Fixed (the historical blind 300 us linger)
arms.off: group commit off (MountOptions default); every sync transaction pays its own barrier

differences: The arms differ ONLY in the group-commit configuration; durability is `sync` in all three.
Latency is the wall time of one write(2)+fsync(2) record, pooled across writers; nearest-rank percentiles.
not_comparable: A grouped arm's `coordinator_barriers` amortises the WRITE barrier only; the application's per-record fsync(2) is a separate barrier the coordinator does not coalesce. Compare barrier FREQUENCY, not raw ops/s alone.
These are single-run figures on one shared host under external load; absolute values move between runs.

detail.note: A write under `sync` is acknowledged only after the batch's shared barrier completes; a fresh daemon then reads every acknowledged record back byte-exact, proving the acknowledgment was not premature.

fault_injection.note: The `durability_barrier` failpoint is armed on the log-level durability hook, so the batch's shared sync fails after every member is published. Every affected append is refused (EIO), never acknowledged.

ordering_detail.note: The coordinator runs each batch's members sequentially, in submission order, against the single authoritative core; the committed sequence is therefore a total order of strictly advancing valid boundaries.

note: MEASURED, NOT SPUN. Three arms of 4 KiB `write+fsync` appends through a real `orfs mount` at 1..64 writers. Grouping turns many per-record barriers into one shared barrier per batch, so the grouped arms scale where the off arm is flat. The application's own `fsync(2)` is still one barrier per record (the coordinator coalesces the write barrier, not the explicit fsync); the receipt reports that frequency explicitly so no reader mistakes the amortisation for a weakened contract. A failed shared barrier is refused, never acknowledged (see `group_commit_barrier_failure_is_refused_not_acknowledged`).
